short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Sharma, 2 runs
commentary: full and straight, searching for the yorker. Rohit clips it to square leg for a couple. The outfield is very, very slow
pre_text:
We're fiddling around with the sightscreen, as we always seem to. About to start though

Looks like Shaheen will bowl the first over. Virat and Rohit walking out to bat.


Meanwhile, as we wait, if you want to hear inspirational stories from other sports, how about this one? Nine months ago, Vinesh Phogat could not even walk. Today, after a gruelling recovery, she is four bouts at the Paris Olympics away from becoming India's greatest-ever wrestler, both on and off the mat.



The teams are walking out for the anthems under somewhat overcast skies.


Ahad: "Danyal, my favourite thing about your commentary is the unveiled disdain towards people writing in. Please never change" It's my favourite thing about doing comms, though I still enjoy people writing in. So keep at it, folks!



Shadow-Shell: "Is it the usual 1 hour extra time for rain delay to complete a full match or is it different for World Cups" There's an extra 90 minutes beyond the usual cut-off times for this game. So they'll try and get a full 40 overs in. There is, just to be clear, no reserve day




BalaBlazer: "Can they allow impact players just for this game? @yuvi and @shahidafridi can join the clash which will make it even more interesting. " Could not imagine a less interesting thing to do




Anant: "Looking forward to the creativity of the ICC in terms of scheduling a reserve game"


It's stopped raining, and the umpires are coming out for an inspection. We will now start at 11.20am local time


Absolutely pouring now, and the start has been delayed


10.41am: It's raining once more


Prashant Vats: "A big toss win for Pakistan. Considering their bowling line up and their never ending habit of ever giving up after loosing to a minnows in a tournament - They are all set to start their tournament with a win over arch rivals!" A lot of you seem to reckon that was a colossal toss to win.



India: Rohit Sharma (capt), Virat Kohli, Rishabh Pant (wk), Suryakumar Yadav, Shivam Dube, Hardik Pandya, Ravindra Jadeja, Axar Patel, Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, Mohammad Siraj

Pakistan: Babar Azam (capt), Mohammad Rizwan (wk), Usman Khan, Fakhar Zaman, Shadab Khan, Iftikhar Ahmed, Imad Wasim, Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf, Naseem Shah, Mohammad Amir



"We've played a few games here, we've tried to assess the conditions as much as possible," Rohit says. "Every game is important. Anything can happen, this is a very funny tournament." India are unchanged 

Pakistan have won the toss and will field first "The past is the past, and we're looking forward to this match," says Babar Azam Imad Wasim in for Azam Khan the only Pakistan change

10.23am Fairly even square boundaries today: 66m on one side and 70m on the other. The wind speed right now is 23kph - not sure what direction it's blowing in. A network of cracks and large plates all over the pitch, with a good amount of grass cover too. Don't expect big totals today.

Tabs: "@james: let's just say that the translation for "Morbo" is weight and baggage of old history"

iPartha: "@James - morbo started on Friday - SL vs Ban has a certain morbo ;) "

10.17am We have news, and it's great news. We'll have a toss at 10.30am, and the match will begin at 11am.

James : "There's a Spanish word, morbo, which has no exact English equivalent. It means history, added interest (for example, Real Madrid vs Barcelona has morbo). There are 2 cricket match ups which, to my mind, have morbo. One is England vs Australia which we had yesterday. The other, particularly because it's only played at world cups, is India vs Pakistan. A weekend of treats!"

10.14am The inspection is on as we speak. The covers are coming off the square.

10.07am Chris Gayle is in New York. Wearing a white jacket that the India players autograph. Just spotted Yuvraj Singh and Sachin Tendulkar too.

Aftab: "Chris Gayle's jacket has Indian colors on right arm and Pakistani colors on left, in case you missed. True legend. This jacket deserves a place in Cricket museum."

10.03am There's an inspection at 10.15am local time

Taz: "I live 10 minutes away from the stadium and I can hear the noise from my porch even though the match hasn't started yet. Insane!!"

Nikhil : "Cricket world cup, rivalry game, tricky pitch and rain delay, this game has to be a psychological nightmare for the players."

Shabbir: "What're the chances of Saim Ayub playing together? He was terrific in the CPL last year but hasn't fired in T20Is yet" Pak have kept team news close to their chest. I suspect he'll miss out today, though


Alosh K Jose: "Got to say, the weather in Paris is perfect for cricket... " They had their fair share of rain in the first week, to be fair


ashish: "@Danyal - you mentioned with some luck the rain might miss the stadium. Looks like you jinxed it right there and the rain decided to take center stage over the stadium." Let's see what else I end up jinxing


9.55am The rain has stopped and the umpires are coming out for an inspection


9.50am The toss has been delayed due to rain. Which, apparently has got lighter, and the Pak players are out training.

Vishwajit Rade : "I'm watching French open final and following Cricinfo !!" You and me both



Meanwhile, if watching another Indian team take on an old foe catches your fancy, the men's hockey team are in action against Great Britain in the FIH Pro League. Follow along for live updates.




9.40am The whole square is covered as the rain gets heavier.. The spectators in the stands don't have cover. 


Diyath: "Um How's the drainage at this ground? I'm not feeling particularly confident given all the other debacles" Apparently not the best, but we might find out today


varun: "I love the commentary but can you make it audible as well? Would be more interesting and user friendly while doing activities such as driving etc." I'd have to shout fairly loudly for you to hear me


9.27am The drizzle is getting slightly more steady now

9.20am Update from Monga at the ground. It's drizzling very, very mildly now.

Fiazleghari.72@: "Hi @Danyal! Have been anxiously refreshing the page for last half an hour or so to check if the coverage has started for this "low-key" contest of the tournament :). First tell us what everybody here wants to know: Which pitch are they going to use (pitch no. 2 or no. 4)" They'll use the strip they used for yesterday's game, the low-scoring thriller that saw South Africa beat the Netherlands.



Vishal: "How's the weather at the ground? It's raining currently a couple hours away in NJ." It's not raining right now, though it is overcast. Think there's a bit of rain expected, though with some luck it might miss the stadium


Have a read of our preview, where George Binoy talks about Pakistan's predicament, and this piece about Pakistan's squad woes from yours truly. Sid Monga, meanwhile, is in New York, who tells us why this hasn't quite captivated the host city as some might have hoped



9am: We begin once more? Has there been a less fancied team in this rivalry in T20I history than Pakistan are against India today? Will that free them up, or does it motivate India to put the 2022 finalists on the verge of elimination in about five hours time? Join us as we begin coverage of these inevitably captivating match-up.

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Sharma, no run
commentary: drags his length back. Rohit defends towards the offside

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Sharma, SIX
commentary: picked up beautifully over the onside. A length ball that he dispatches way over the midwicket boundary. Caught it sweetly out of the middle and it flies away for a huge six

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Sharma, no run
commentary: wider outside off at just under 137kph. The batter watches it through to the keeper

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Sharma, no run
commentary: shaping away, this one. Slightly fuller. Rohit prods it to the offside

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Sharma, no run
commentary: huge appeal from the bowlers, but Babar reckons there's a faint inside edge, and doesn't review. If there wasn't one, that was probably plumb in front

short_text: Naseem Shah to Kohli, FOUR
commentary: a bit of outswing, but it's a half-volley, and the swing only gives Kohli width to free his arms and drive sweetly to the right of cover. Travels quickly even on this outfield
pre_text: 11.58am Aaaaand we're good to go again. Virat Kohli on strike for the first time today, and he'll be facing Naseem Shah. Slip and a gully in place.

short_text: Naseem Shah to Kohli, no run
commentary: length ball, top of off, gets his weight moving nicely into the ball to defend it back to the bowler

short_text: Naseem Shah to Kohli, OUT
commentary: width again, but Kohli has slapped this straight to cover point! On the shorter side of a length, a bit of shape away, and Kohli ends up having to reach for the ball, and toe-ends it to Usman, who catches it two-handed over his head. Don't know if the ball stuck in the pitch a little, or if it was just the wide-ness of the line that made Kohli hit it not quite off the middle
dismissal: V Kohli c Usman Khan b Naseem Shah 4 (7m 3b 1x4 0x6) SR: 133.33

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pant, no run
commentary: Lovely delivery, slanted across the stumps but finishing close to off, on a good length. Pant presses forward to defend, playing for swing into him, and it keeps going with the angle, or seams away, and beats his outside edge
pre_text: Rishabh Pant is in at No. 3. Naseem stays over the wicket to the left-hander.

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pant, 2 wides
commentary: full, swinging down the leg side. Pant misses the flick, and the diving Rizwan stops the ball - which bounces again in front of him - but lets it run away from him a little, allowing India to steal another run

short_text: Naseem Shah to Sharma, FOUR
commentary: overpitched, too straight, ends up right up at Rohit's toes. Fine leg is in the circle, and Rohit clips it neatly into the big gap to his left

short_text: Naseem Shah to Sharma, 1 run
commentary: length ball close to off stump, lets it come and steers to deep third

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Sharma, no run
commentary: fullish, slanting across Rohit, gets forward and defends towards midwicket
pre_text:
Shaheen will continue. Left-arm over.

Mannu: "That was such Sehwagesque dismissal!!"

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Sharma, no run
commentary: fullish, not quite up for the drive, slanting away from off stump. Rohit looks to drive on the up, possibly playing for a bit of swing into him. Keeps going with the angle and beats him

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Sharma, no run
commentary: length ball slanting across, finishing in the close corridor. Looks to defend with soft hands, gets an edge that bounces well short of slip diving right

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Sharma, OUT
commentary: there's that pick-up shot again, but this time he's picked out the fielder at deep square leg! I think Rohit has been done in again by the lack of swing. It was quite full, quite straight, but I would think Rohit was aiming to hit behind square, but it ends up coming off the face of his bat a little awkwardly, and goes to the man on the boundary, who moves a few yards to his left to take it. The ball may have stopped on Rohit too
dismissal: RG Sharma c Haris Rauf b Shaheen Shah Afridi 13 (15m 12b 1x4 1x6) SR: 108.33

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Patel, 1 wide
commentary: full, wide outside off, left alone. Wide signalled. Ended up just beyond the tramline
pre_text: Wow. Axar Patel is in at No. 4! Two left-handers in now.

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Patel, no run
commentary: length ball close to off stump, punched to cover

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Patel, no run
commentary: length ball finishing close to the top of middle stump. Stays a little leg side of the ball and defends with soft hands towards backward point

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Pant, no run
commentary: fullish, swinging away fairly wide of off, left alone
pre_text: Amir. Left-arm over.

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Pant, 3 runs
commentary: full, angling in, finishing close to off stump, and Pant gets his head on top of the ball and flicks it to the left of mid-on. The slowness of the outfield allows Shaheen to chase back and pull it back in front of the boundary

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Patel, no run
commentary: swing! Nice length in the corridor, and it leaves the left-hander pretty late. Looks to drive on the up through the covers and is beaten

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Patel, no run
commentary: swing again, but from a shorter length. Axar is beaten again, this time he's looking to cut

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Patel, no run
commentary: beaten for the third time in a row. Extravagant swing this time, from a full length that's not quite a driving length. The line is outside off, inviting the drive, but Axar isn't putting bat to this one. Swung a LOT

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Patel, 1 run
commentary: very full outside off, opens his bat face and squeezes it down to third
pre_text: Deep third and deep square leg are the two fielders back. Slip in place too.

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Patel, FOUR
commentary: length ball outside off, and Axar looks to get low for a flat-bat square drive. Ends up getting a thick edge that races away wide of slip
pre_text: Shaheen. Third over in the powerplay.

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Patel, SIX
commentary: shot. Shaheen goes short now, and he gets it to climb steeply just outside off. Axar lets it come, and ramps it smartly over slip, an d gets it to carry all the way for six. Lovely bit of timing

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Patel, 1 run
commentary: full outside off, Axar doesn't quite gets his weight forward into the drive, hits it a little uppishly, but it's in the gap to the right of cover

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Pant, no run
commentary: full outside off, a bit of away-swing. Driven to cover point

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Pant, 1 run
commentary: length ball close to off stump, and it nips back into Pant off the pitch. Looks to dab it square on the off side, and gets a thick inside edge past his leg stump
pre_text:
Pant backs away just as Shaheen jumps into his delivery stride. Someone walked in front of the sightscreen.

James : "Beautiful stuff from Amir. I remember seeing him do that in a test at Old Trafford some years ago. "

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Patel, 2 runs
commentary: length ball outside off, gets down on his back knee for a back-cut to the left of deep third. Good, aggressive running to pick up two

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Pant, FOUR
commentary: thick edge, and it just eludes slip! Full outside off, swinging away, and Pant goes hard at the front-foot drive. Iftikhar throws himself to his left at slip, and it's going quite high too. Can't quite get his hands to it
pre_text:
Ghaffar: "Looks like a 160 pitch and best pitch of New york this event." --- Certainly seems like it so far. 

Axar has changed his pads. Now Amir continues.

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Pant, 3 runs
commentary: it's all happening. Now Usman Khan puts down a tough chance. Full again, starting on the stumps and swinging away from Pant. Was looking to whip it over the leg side, ends up sending a leading edge ballooning over the off side. Usman turns around at cover point and chases with the ball dropping from over his shoulder, and he gets his hands to it but can't hold on

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Patel, no run
commentary: Amir is bowling beautifully here. Length ball nips in from just outside off. Presses forward to defend, and it sneaks through the gate but bounces over the stumps

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Patel, 1 run
commentary: length ball close to off stump, gets forward and dabs to backward point

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Pant, FOUR
commentary: four more, and again it's off the edge. What a bittersweet over for Amir. Again it's full, swinging away from the stumps, and again Pant goes hard, looking to whip over the leg side. This time the edge flies high over slip

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Pant, no run
commentary: fullish outside off, Pant goes for the drive, and it swings away and beats him. No luck at all for Amir. Not much bounce this time, bounces again before reaching Rizwan

short_text: Iftikhar Ahmed to Patel, no run
commentary: comes around the wicket, defended back to the  bowler
pre_text: Right, how are we looking now? Who's powerplay was that, do we think?

short_text: Iftikhar Ahmed to Patel, 1 run
commentary: angling in flat, eased through to point for a single

short_text: Iftikhar Ahmed to Pant, no run
commentary: tries to pick it up over fine leg but misses. Perhaps it clipped the pad because it's not called wide

short_text: Iftikhar Ahmed to Pant, no run
commentary: inside edge nearly chopped onto the stumps. Pant tried to pick it up over fine leg but the shot was never really on
pre_text: Vamsi Krishna B: "India's power play for sure. considering the moisture in the air, and generally how the pitches in this ground has played."

short_text: Iftikhar Ahmed to Pant, 1 wide
commentary: flat and wide down leg

short_text: Iftikhar Ahmed to Pant, 1 run
commentary: came down the wicket so Iftikhar drags his length back. Eased to long-on

short_text: Iftikhar Ahmed to Patel, FOUR
commentary: finishes the over with a boundary. Dances down the track and drives him over his head for four. Gun barrel straight, and he rescues the over for India somewhat

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pant, 1 run
commentary: thick inside edge to midwicket and they come through for a single
pre_text: Bilal Anwar: "Excellent over that from Amir but without any luck. Hopefully, luck favors him in his last two overs ." Phenomenally unlucky over, yep

short_text: Naseem Shah to Patel, no run
commentary: length ball outside off stump, driven on the up to mid-off

short_text: Naseem Shah to Patel, no run
commentary: length delivery once more, defended back to the bowler

short_text: Naseem Shah to Patel, OUT
commentary: cleans him up! Axar danced down the wicket but misses a straight one which crashes into the stumps. The pressure had built after a good over and a half from Pakistan since the PP and this shot was never really on. Pakistan have the wicket they'll feel they deserve
pre_text: Shyam: "Can someone remind Pant there is no impact sub"
dismissal: AR Patel  b Naseem Shah 20 (26m 18b 2x4 1x6) SR: 111.11

short_text: Naseem Shah to Yadav, no run
commentary: length ball, SKY prods at it towards the offside

short_text: Naseem Shah to Yadav, FOUR
commentary: splits mid-off and mid-on with a crackling straight drive! Ends the over with a boundary once more, and they salvage something from it. It was slightly overpitched, allowing SKY to lean into that drive

short_text: Imad Wasim to Pant, 1 wide
pre_text: Khan: "Ramiz Raja jixed Axar there on live comms. He said India's highest score at number 4 against Pakistan is 20 and look what happens next ball."

short_text: Imad Wasim to Pant, 1 run
commentary: topedged and an inrushing Usman cannot take the catch! Didn't get to the pitch of the ball, Pant, and sent it straight up, but gets lucky as it's just far enough away from Usman

short_text: Imad Wasim to Yadav, 1 run
commentary: grips and turns, SKY pokes it to short third and gets off strike

short_text: Imad Wasim to Pant, no run
Imad Wasim to Pant, no run
commentary: Pant trying too much. Attempts another reverse pick-up that's never on and gets nowhere near it

short_text: Imad Wasim to Pant, 2 runs
commentary: heaved into the onside and they race through for a couple

short_text: Imad Wasim to Pant, 1 run
commentary: slaps it to mid-on, doesn't time it yet again, and it falls short of the fielder

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pant, no run
commentary: comes around the wicket, length delivery. Defended back to the bowler
pre_text: Prince: "Has Pant middled anything yet? Never seen something like this" The luckier a batter gets, the more you wonder if it's their day, though. And Pant's still there

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pant, FOUR
commentary: slower ball, and Pant waits for it. Hits it through the line up and over extra cover, and it runs away for four

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pant, FOUR
commentary: falls over as he laps it past fine leg, using the pace of the ball to help it to the boundary. That shot is not in the manual, but Pant finds a way of steering it into the precise gap he wants

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pant, FOUR
commentary: comes back over the wicket but it's on the pads, and Pant flicks it past fine leg once more Haris's pace means he can't afford to err in line

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pant, 1 run
commentary: carved it towards third man and they come through for one

short_text: Haris Rauf to Yadav, no run
commentary: decent delivery to finish off the over. Over 142 kph, and it beats the limply hanging bat of Suryakumar

short_text: Imad Wasim to Pant, 1 run
commentary: smeared towards square leg and they ease through for a single
pre_text:
Fiaz Laghari: "Why would you remove Naseem Shah from the attack just after he got a wicket? Pant was also not feeling confident against him. Babar's captaincy is always strange."


Abdul Rasheed : "Both Haris and Shadab could have made ways for Abbas Afridi and Abrar"

short_text: Imad Wasim to Yadav, 1 run
commentary: drags it down leg and they come through for the extra run
pre_text: Hamza: "@Abdul Rasheed except Abbas Afridi isn't in the squad" He is

short_text: Imad Wasim to Pant, no run
commentary: bottom handed jab attempted but it kept slightly low

short_text: Imad Wasim to Pant, FOUR
commentary: reverse sweep picked up over the man at 45 at it races away. After that early fortune, he's now settling into his trademark, ominous self

short_text: Imad Wasim to Pant, 1 run
commentary: comes down the wicket and clips it towards cow corner

short_text: Imad Wasim to Yadav, 1 run
commentary: punched down to long-off

short_text: Haris Rauf to Yadav, no run
commentary: tailed in and rapped him on the pads. Muffled appeal from the bowler but it was clearly heading down leg

short_text: Haris Rauf to Yadav, OUT
commentary: scoops it up straight to Amir at mid-off! Yadav never really appeared to catch that as he spliced it into the air, and he can't clear mid-off. Pakistan have a breakthrough, if not the man they desperately want
pre_text: Malik: "Considering the current mindset of Team Pak, 150 on board and 2 early wickets in 2nd innings, means bye bye pakistan for today. "
dismissal: SA Yadav c Mohammad Amir b Haris Rauf 7 (16m 8b 1x4 0x6) SR: 87.5

short_text: Haris Rauf to Dube, no run
commentary: length ball outside off, hung his bat out, no feet, beaten.

short_text: Haris Rauf to Dube, no run
commentary: length ball to Dube, who defends it back to Rauf

short_text: Haris Rauf to Dube, no run
commentary: back of a length from Haris, reared up slightly. Defended into the offside

short_text: Haris Rauf to Dube, 1 run
commentary: carved away through to point and it's a single that prevents a wicket maiden

short_text: Imad Wasim to Dube, 1 run
commentary: eased into the onside to get Pant back on strike
pre_text: SR: "Sky form is a big issue. Maybe either bring him down or replace with Sanju Samson"

short_text: Imad Wasim to Pant, 1 run
commentary: spun sharply back in as he steers it to square leg

short_text: Imad Wasim to Dube, no run
commentary: slapped back to the bowler

short_text: Imad Wasim to Dube, 1 run
commentary: grips off the surface once more as its whipped into the inside

short_text: Imad Wasim to Pant, 1 leg bye
commentary: tried to lob it over short third but it hits the pad and they come through for a legbye

short_text: Imad Wasim to Dube, no run
commentary: skids this one through and it's driven back to the bowler

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pant, 1 run
commentary: opens the face and runs it down to third man
pre_text: MV33: "Danyal, how's the weather forecast?" Clear for the rest of the match

short_text: Naseem Shah to Dube, OUT
commentary: grips in the pitch slightly and it's scooped up to Naseem Shah, who has his third wicket! he did not read that slower ball, got stuck on the crease and just shovelled at it with his hands. Naseem will never have an easier catch off his own bowling, and Pakistan are suddenly rampant
dismissal: S Dube c & b Naseem Shah 3 (7m 9b 0x4 0x6) SR: 33.33

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pandya, no run
pre_text:
Salman Lalwani: "So Shadab is playing as a batsmen today?" Looks that way. Hard to blame Pakistan for that though


Adway Lele : "I wonder if Surya and Dube are right selections for American leg of world cup. With spicey pitches, Surya is neutralized and Dube is not required to disrupt spin either. Both these players should be handy in Caribbean. "

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pandya, no run
commentary: comes down the wicket and slaps it uppishly towards the general direction of mid-off, but it bounces before it gets there

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pandya, no run
commentary: length ball defended back down the ground
pre_text: Ray Vermont: "Has the pitch changed or is it poor shot selection from the batsmen. Pakistan have completely turned it around. " To be fair I think Pakistan were quite unlucky in the phase before the clump of wickets well

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pandya, 1 no ball
commentary: drags this one down leg and the umpire calls it wide. Oh, wait, it's a no-ball! Naseem overstepped, and India have a free hit

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pandya, no run
commentary: Pandya swings like a rusty gate and misses. Naseem gets away with it, and it's a phenomenally good over - two runs and a wicket

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Pant, OUT
commentary: straight up in the air and Pant falls too! Babar takes an easy catch. India are imploding here  It stuck in the pitch and Pant went high rather than long, and Babar came across from mid-off to take a simple catch
dismissal: RR Pant c Babar Azam b Mohammad Amir 42 (65m 31b 6x4 0x6) SR: 135.48

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Jadeja, OUT
commentary: Jadeja goes first ball! This is carnage. Pakistan fans are making all the noise in New York. Just dabbed at one that floated up to Imad at short mid-off, and Amir is off and away! He'll be on a hat-trick and India's middle order has been cut to ribbons
pre_text: Sulait : "Ball still moving around a bit for naseem. India is in good position rn with most of their seem ballers are like naseem" Yeah, you reckon no chase will be straightforward on this surface
dismissal: RA Jadeja c Imad Wasim b Mohammad Amir 0 (1m 1b 0x4 0x6) SR: 0

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Arshdeep Singh, no run
commentary: length ball, Arshdeep gets in line and defends
pre_text: George: "Not a single Indian batsman has looked comfortable on this wicket. Even Pant's 42 was largely due to huge slices of luck."

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Arshdeep Singh, 1 run
commentary: gets across and clips it to fine leg for a single

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Pandya, no run
commentary: slower ball, and Hardik lets this one go

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Pandya, no run
commentary: lets another one go. Two wickets and one run in that over. On that note, I hand it to Karthik to finish the innings off
pre_text: Sudhir: "Ridiculous performance from India here. "Imploding" is an understatement. All shots that has gotten wickets have either been clueless batting, lack of awareness, inability to read the pitch or just plain over-confidence and arrogance."

short_text: Naseem Shah to Arshdeep Singh, no run
commentary: length ball slanting across, a little late getting forward to defend and it slides past the outside edge
pre_text: Thanks, Danyal. Can India bat out their 20? Here's Naseem again. Over the wicket to the left-handed Arshdeep.

short_text: Naseem Shah to Arshdeep Singh, 1 run
commentary: back of a length, angling away into the corridor, opens the bat face to steer to deep third
pre_text: Only four back on the boundary, and a man at slip.

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: fullish, close to off stump, steps across first and then gets forward for a push towards mid-off, who's on the edge of the circle

short_text: Naseem Shah to Arshdeep Singh, no run
commentary: banged in short, angling across the left-hander. Late on the hook, and he doesn't get any bat on it

short_text: Naseem Shah to Arshdeep Singh, no run
commentary: and there's the yorker, slower one too, 116kph in the blockhole. Dug out square on the off side

short_text: Naseem Shah to Arshdeep Singh, 1 run
commentary: shuffles across to this length ball slanting into the sixth-stump channel, and clips it wide of mid-on

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Arshdeep Singh, FOUR
commentary: Arshdeep heaves one away. Length ball slanting in towards off stump, and he just stands there, opens up his hips, and clubs it away over wide mid-on. Doesn't quite nail it, and it lands and slows down in the outfield, but enough impetus on the ball to pick up four
pre_text:
Amir to finish off. Left-arm over.

Din: "No disrespect to Pak, but I don't see they chasing anything above 130 in this pitch against Bumrah and co bowling. " -- 130 is still quite a way away...

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Arshdeep Singh, no run
commentary: length ball just outside off, hangs back and defends into the covers

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Arshdeep Singh, no run
commentary: did that carry? Doesn't matter, because Rizwan hasn't held on. And it's hurt Arshdeep. Cross-seam bouncer, and Arshdeep gets into an awkward, cramped position while trying to hook. Jams his right glove into his bat handle, and then loops up behind the wicket, teasingly. Rizwan has to throw himself forward to try and catch it, and I don't think it carried. Can't catch it on the bounce either

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Arshdeep Singh, 2 runs
commentary: full, angling in towards off stump, opens his hips and swipes it away through midwicket. Deep square leg moves to his right to stop it
pre_text: Arshdeep is okay to continue. India will be glad it's his non-bowling hand.

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Arshdeep Singh, no run
commentary: again, an edge doesn't carry. Steps out and Amir bowls a cutter into the pitch, the line just outside off. Swings across the line, gets an edge to it, but it falls well short of the keeper

short_text: Mohammad Amir to Arshdeep Singh, no run
commentary: wow. Arshdeep takes stance outside leg stump, a long way outside, exposing all his stumps, then jumps across before the bowler delivers. Ends up going full but outside off, and Arshdeep swings and misses, aiming leg side

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, FOUR
commentary: shortish, angling into the stumps, and Hardik makes room, exposes all his stumps, and rolls his wrists over a back-cut. Thick edge, flies very fine, and the diving deep third, moving to his left, can't cut it off. Naseem seems to hurt his right knee while diving there
pre_text: Rauf.

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, no run
commentary: back of a length, nips in to hit the thigh pad as Hardik misses the tuck off his legs

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, 2 runs
commentary: another thick edge, and this time Shadab is back at deep third, and he stops this from reaching the boundary. Similar to the previous boundary, shortish ball that Hardik makes room against and flashes at. Not quite as short as the previous one, and a terrific bit of work from Shadab, throws himself full-length to his left

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, OUT
commentary: taken, Ifti on the leg-side boundary! Length ball angling into the stumps, and Hardik shuffles across and looks for the pick-up flick. Hits it pretty well, but Iftikhar, sprinting left from long leg, intercepts it nicely
dismissal: HH Pandya c Iftikhar Ahmed b Haris Rauf 7 (24m 12b 1x4 0x6) SR: 58.33

short_text: Haris Rauf to Bumrah, OUT
commentary: and he's gone first ball. Full and wide, and Bumrah gets a nice stride in to drive, and he hits it well, but hits it in the air, at chest height, straight to Imad at short cover. India nine down
pre_text: Bumrah is in at No. 10.
dismissal: JJ Bumrah c Imad Wasim b Haris Rauf 0 (1m 1b 0x4 0x6) SR: 0

short_text: Haris Rauf to Mohammed Siraj, 1 run
commentary: looks for the yorker, ends up angling slightly down leg. Steps across and clips to deep square leg
pre_text: Rauf is on a hat-trick now, with Mohammed Siraj in his sights. Slip in place.

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Mohammed Siraj, 2 runs
commentary: in the blockhole, slanting across to finish jusy outside off. Jabbed to the right of backward point, where Shadab sprints to the ball and throws at the keeper's end, conceding an overthrow
pre_text:
Shaheen to bowl his fourth. Over the wicket.

Deep Bhatia: "This is what happens when you have such batting pitches in the IPL with super short boundaries. Most of the Indian batsmen have perished either getting flummoxed by the pace of the pitch or holing out in the deep."

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Mohammed Siraj, 2 runs
commentary: fullish outside off, plays a checked drive to the right of deep point
pre_text: Round the wicket now.

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Mohammed Siraj, 2 runs
commentary: low full-toss outside off, jabbed towards that deep cover fielder again, and Siraj sprinted out for a second, so the fielder throws at his end as he hurries back that way. Not the best of throws, and the bowler can't collect cleanly either - he may have been unsighted by Siraj running across him - and India get another overthrow

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Mohammed Siraj, no run
commentary: now Siraj steps across his stumps, aiming for a scoop/deflection over short fine leg. Shaheen goes on pace, length, at the stumps, and beats the batter but it bounces over the stumps

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Mohammed Siraj, no run
commentary: looks to step across and scoop again. This time it's fuller and outside off, and he misses again, or does he get a little touch on it? Pakistan appeal for caught behind, and it's not given. Babar has reviewed... Cross-seam ball, and did it brush the face of the bat as it went? Close, but no contact. Nothing on Ultra Edge

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Mohammed Siraj, OUT
commentary: ooh, driven in the air, but it doesn't carry to mid-off. But Pakistan get their wicket anyway, because there's a mix-up. Full, angling in towards leg stump, following Siraj's attempt to create room. Drives and almost yorks Babar at mid-off. He picks up and throws to the keeper's end, because while Siraj set off immediately, Arshdeep was slow to respond. Nowhere in the picture as Rizwan collects and whips off the bails. India are bowled out with an over to spare

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Mohammad Rizwan, 3 runs
commentary: full and wide. Rizwan leans into a drive. Hardik has a chase on his hands as the pair run three
pre_text:
Looks like Arshdeep Singh will open the bowling, while Babar and Rizwan come out to bat

Right, folks, we're just about to get underway. Pakistan need exactly a run a ball to resurrect their campaign on a pitch that, let's be honest, no one knows how to read

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Babar Azam, 3 runs
commentary: full once more, and sliced through the covers from Babar as well. A pair of threes to start off the innings

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: thick inside edge, nearly chopped it on. Runs down to fine leg and the pair exchange ends

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Babar Azam, 2 wides
commentary: gets his line wrong and the keeper can't collect cleanly, so they come through for an extra wide

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: tailing back into the pads, driven to mid-on

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: back of a length delivery, Rizwan dabs it to backward point

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: bit of shape in, and it's driven to cover-point, where Kohli collects smartly

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Babar Azam, FOUR
commentary: driven down the ground and it sneaks underneath a diving mid-on. Classy drive from the Pakistan captain, and it brings up the Pakistanis' first boundary
pre_text: zubair Rashid: "hey cricinfo! was this the first the two openers opened their score card with 3's? " I was wondering the same

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Babar Azam, 1 run
commentary: thick outside edge runs down to third man for a single

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: what a beauty! Landed on length and seamed away, inches away from Rizwan's outside edge. The batter was opened up but doesn't get the edge

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: punched to backward point for no run

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: clipped to midwicket, where it's fielded sharply. Decent comeback from Siraj after the first ball

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: driven back to Siraj, who collects and then wallops Rizwan with the ball in his attempt to run him out. Rizwan doesn't look especially pleased, but they hug it out

short_text: Bumrah to Mohammad Rizwan, 2 runs

short_text: Bumrah to Mohammad Rizwan, no run

short_text: Bumrah to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: looked to pick it up outside off stump to smear it towards cow corner. Gets a thick inside edge onto his body
pre_text: Arjun: "Rizwan is standing so front of wicket. This negates some swing. This tactics and game awareness was missing with India."

short_text: Bumrah to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: Rizwan slapped it straight to Dube at fine leg, where he puts down an absolute sitter! How costly could that be! He didn't have to move, but ends up shelling it

short_text: Bumrah to Babar Azam, 1 run
commentary: thick outside edge to third man

short_text: Bumrah to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: driven down to mid-off for no run. Bumrah unlucky that over

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Babar Azam, no run
commentary: slapped back to Siraj, and it's popped out of his hands! Those are the kinds that sometimes stick in the follow-through, but it didn't, and then lands harmlessly from Pakistan's point of view

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Babar Azam, no run
commentary: back of a length, defended into the onside

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Babar Azam, 1 leg bye
commentary: clipped off the pads and they come through for a single
pre_text: Sundeep: "Remember those negating swing tactics comes from Gary Kirsten. He got India last world cup."

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: length ball again, hits the inner half of the bat as it rolls to midwicket

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: back of a length, Rizwan dabs it towards first slip, but no run. India have managed to apply something of a squeeze here

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: tucked into the onside and they scurry through for a single

short_text: Bumrah to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: back of a length, cross-batted steer from Rizwan to get off strike
pre_text: Conrad Dodd: "Rizwan falls over seemingly much of the time he plays forward. Surely pitch it up to him and make him play the drive or angle in at the stumps so LB in play? " Bumrah might try it in the upcoming over

short_text: Bumrah to Babar Azam, no run
commentary: crunched toward point, but it's straight to the fielder

short_text: Bumrah to Babar Azam, FOUR
commentary: back of a length ball. Babar read the length early and slapped it over long-on; the ball runs away to the boundary
pre_text: Mohyuddin: "People are talking about tactics but reality is Rizwan consumed a lot of balls and still not comfortable which is very concerning."

short_text: Bumrah to Babar Azam, OUT
commentary: Bumrah strikes! Sensational catch in the slips. Length ball that shaped back in; Babar wasn't sure whether to play or leave, ends up dabbing it to Suryakumar Yadav at first slip, where it looks like the catch is taken. They're double checking though, but the fingers do look like they're underneath the ball. It's officially confirmed, and India have their first
dismissal: Babar Azam c Yadav b Bumrah 13 (23m 10b 2x4 0x6) SR: 130

short_text: Bumrah to Usman Khan, no run
commentary: nearly had two in two. Whizzes past the outside edge as Haris drove unconvincingly

short_text: Bumrah to Usman Khan, no run
commentary: beats the outside edge once again. Muffled appeal from the Indians, but it missed the edge again. Usman thankul to get out of the over

short_text: Pandya to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: driven towards long-off. Usman looked for a run but Rizwan sent him back
pre_text: Safdar: "I've a TV at home and i am too faint hearted to watch it live. Cricinfo is my refuge. "

short_text: Pandya to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: clipped to long-on as Rizwan fell over slightly

short_text: Pandya to Mohammad Rizwan, SIX
commentary: dances down the track and slaps it over extra cover for a 74m six. That breaks the shackles somewhat for Pakistan after India had begun to dry the runs up

short_text: Pandya to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run

short_text: Pandya to Usman Khan, 1 wide

short_text: Pandya to Usman Khan, 1 run
commentary: length ball from Pandya, clipped towards mid-on. Pakistan scurry through for another one

short_text: Pandya to Mohammad Rizwan, no run

pre_text: Manoj Kumar: "why aren't they playing as many Pakistani songs in the stadium?" I can make out a few

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Usman Khan, no run
commentary: struck him slightly high on the bat to mid-off
pre_text: Abubakar: "I made a pact to shut off tv after babar. Cricinfo with eyes only on wicket column." Well, you're very welcome here!

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Usman Khan, no run
commentary: angling back in and Usman misses once more. It's an uncertain start from him here

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Usman Khan, 1 run
commentary: bouncer that Usman took eyes off and worked to midwicket to get himself off strike

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Usman Khan, no run

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Usman Khan, 1 run
Jadeja to Usman Khan, 1 run
commentary: around the wicket, steered to square leg for a single
pre_text: Sam: "Usman Khan seems out of his depth here." It has been a meteoric rise for a player who wasn't even a Pakistan player until a few months ago

short_text: Jadeja to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: length ball, defended to extra cover
pre_text: Vijit Mahaur: "If Pakistan play 20 overs, it'll be all over for India. India need wickets and they need them fast."

short_text: Jadeja to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: nudged into the onside and gets a single

short_text: Jadeja to Usman Khan, 1 run

short_text: Jadeja to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: rapped on the pads and Rizwan nearly set off for one before Usman wisely sends him back

short_text: Jadeja to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: worked to long-off and Rizwan keeps the strike

short_text: Pandya to Mohammad Rizwan, no run

short_text: Pandya to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: eased to fine leg for one

short_text: Pandya to Usman Khan, FOUR
commentary: comes down the track and slaps Pandya over cover for four. Flat-batted this one and caught it out of the middle as it races away for Pakistan's first post Powerplay boundary

short_text: Pandya to Usman Khan, 2 runs
commentary: whipped off the pads to midwicket for another couple

short_text: Pandya to Usman Khan, 1 run
commentary: bouncer from Pandya which is pulled away for another single
pre_text: Amir: "Worst strategy from Pakistan. Why you are playing so slow. Can't you dare to finish 3or 4 balls earlier "

short_text: Pandya to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: slower delivery, but Rizwan read it. Nudged towards midwicket and he keeps the strike. Nine off the over
pre_text: Niraj : "Stage is set for second wicket. Come on India "

short_text: Jadeja to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: carved to short third uppishly. Well fielded there
pre_text: Saket: "I say that india should not leak runs in order to take wickets now. Bowl tight overs, once RRR is over 8, Pakistan will panic, and give you wickets."

short_text: Jadeja to Usman Khan, 1 run
commentary: punched past point. Pakistan thought about two but Dube in the deep was sharp enough to dispel that thought

short_text: Jadeja to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: a bit of grip and it beats Rizwan. The keeper whips off the bails but Rizwan's in his crease

short_text: Jadeja to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: loses his balance as he defends back to the bowler

short_text: Jadeja to Mohammad Rizwan, no run
commentary: carved to point, but it's cut off

short_text: Jadeja to Mohammad Rizwan, FOUR
commentary: lovely inside out drive. Came down the wicket and lofted it over the cover region, just wide enough of long-off. Breaks the shackles as the teams break for drinks. Pakistan in charge at the halfway stage, and I leave you with Karthik for the rest of this game

short_text: Patel to Usman Khan, OUT
commentary: there's that Axar slider going with that big inward angle from wide of the crease. Goes on the back foot, presumably looking to play through the off side, and it hurries on with the angle and he hurriedly jams his bat down. Can't connect, and it beats the inside edge to hit the back pad. Huge lbw appeal, not given, and India have reviewed... It's struck him in front of middle stump, he's on the back foot, the ball doesn't have a long way to go, and HawkEye says it's crashing into a good chunk of leg stump. Axar has struck first ball!!!
pre_text: Thanks, Danyal. Pakistan have a win probability of above 96% at the moment, according to our Forecaster. India need a couple of wickets in a hurry. Can Axar Patel bring them one? Here he is, left-arm around.
dismissal: Usman Khan lbw b Patel 13 (23m 15b 1x4 0x6) SR: 86.66

short_text: Patel to Fakhar Zaman, 1 run

pre_text: Fakhar Zaman is in at No. 3. Left-hander vs left-arm orthodox. Axar goes over the wicket, and puts a slip in.

short_text: Patel to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: full, angling into the pads, clipped to the right of midwicket
pre_text: Round the wicket to the RHB.

short_text: Patel to Fakhar Zaman, SIX

pre_text: Over the wicket to Fakhar.

short_text: Patel to Fakhar Zaman, no run

short_text: Patel to Fakhar Zaman, 1 run

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Fakhar Zaman, FOUR
commentary: they need less than a run a ball now. Poor ball, full and angling down leg, and Fakhar flicks and gets just enough bat on it to get it into the gap fine of short fine
pre_text: Pakistan are going at exactly a run a ball, and they need exactly a run a ball. Arshdeep returns, left-arm over.

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Fakhar Zaman, no run
commentary: length ball straightens towards off stump, squares up a little while defending into the covers

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Fakhar Zaman, 1 run
commentary: full outside off, weight not fully forward to drive, plays it in the air but in the gap to the left of backward point

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Mohammad Rizwan, no run

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Mohammad Rizwan, no run

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: shortish, gets up to Rizwan's hip. Swats it round to long leg

short_text: Pandya to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: slower ball, fairly full and angling into the stumps, clipped towards deep square leg
pre_text: Will India persist with the left-arm spinner with Fakhar at the crease? They don't. Hardik returns, after two expensive overs.

short_text: Pandya to Fakhar Zaman, OUT
commentary: got him, Hardik gets a big wicket, and Pant takes a terrific catch! Steps out and Hardik bounces him. Well directed, at the front shoulder, cramps him for room, and he only manages to glove his pull. It loops up over Pant's right shoulder, and his weight is initially moving left, because of Hardik's angle. He does so well to turn around, run backwards, mindful of the helmet behind him, and then complete a terrific falling, tumbling catch
pre_text:
Hardik stays over the wicket to the LHB.

Kunal : "BBB - Bring Back Bumrah"
dismissal: Fakhar Zaman c †Pant b Pandya 13 (8m 8b 1x4 1x6) SR: 162.5

short_text: Pandya to Imad Wasim, no run

pre_text: Another left-hander. Here's Imad Wasim. Stays over the wicket.

short_text: Pandya to Imad Wasim, no run

short_text: Pandya to Imad Wasim, no run

pre_text: Round the wicket now.

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 leg bye
commentary: back of a length, straightens into the thigh pad with extra bounce. Looks to hop and flick, only manages thigh pad into the off side
pre_text: Arshdeep to bowl his third. Left-arm over.

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Imad Wasim, FOUR

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Imad Wasim, no run

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Imad Wasim, 1 run
commentary: shortish at the hip, tucked away to fine leg

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Mohammad Rizwan, 1 run
commentary: length ball straightens a touch, in towards off stump. Punched off the back foot to long-off

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Imad Wasim, no run

short_text: Bumrah to Mohammad Rizwan, OUT

pre_text: Stays over the wicket to Imad.

pre_text: Stays over the wicket to Imad.

short_text: Pandya to Imad Wasim, 1 run
commentary: 2-6 now, and he'll finish with 2-24. What an effort. Looks to make room again, and Hardik bowls a fullish offcutter that finishes around off stump. Swiped along the ground to long-on
pre_text: Hardik has 2-5 from his last 1.5 overs.

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Imad Wasim, 1 run
commentary: length ball finishing on top of off stump, makes room and slaps to deep point
pre_text:
Three overs to go. It'll be Siraj to bowl this, and I guess Bumrah the 19th and Arshdeep the 20th. Pakistan need 30. Ten an over. Hardik goes off the field, and Samson comes on as a sub.

Siraj over the wicket to the LHB.

Joe: "This is turning from slow burner into a cliffhanger."

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Iftikhar Ahmed, 1 no ball
commentary: full, angling into the stumps. Almost a yorker. Wristily drilled back down the ground, and it hits the stumps at the other end. And... uh oh, Siraj has overstepped. Not by a lot, but a no-ball nonmetheless.
pre_text: Short third, short fine leg.

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Iftikhar Ahmed, 2 runs
commentary: back of a length outside off, flat-batted to the right of deep point

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Iftikhar Ahmed, 1 run
commentary: back of a length outside off, chopped to the right of backward point

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Imad Wasim, 1 run
commentary: looks to make room again and Siraj slants an attempted yorker out towards off stump. Low full-toss, steered to deep point

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Iftikhar Ahmed, 1 wide
commentary: slower bouncer, ends up looping down the leg side, as Iftikhar pulls out of the pull

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Iftikhar Ahmed, 1 run
commentary: hard length, angling in towards leg stump. No room at all, and Iftikhar pushes with a straight bat into the vacant midwicket region. Siraj does the chasing himself

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Imad Wasim, 1 run
commentary: good ball to finish the over, low full-toss at the base of the stumps. Driven back down the ground off the low part of the bat, and Siraj, falling down in his follow-through, can't quite prevent it from rolling down to long-on for one

short_text: Bumrah to Imad Wasim, 1 run
commentary: offcutter grips like an offbreak. Into the pitch, pitches well outside leg stump and ends up the other side of Imad's  body as he tries to make room. Then ends up jabbing at it and gets a thick edge that rolls towards short third
pre_text: 21 from 12. Here is Bumrah. Over the wicket.

short_text: Bumrah to Iftikhar Ahmed, no run
commentary: slower short ball, and again it turns like an offbreak. Amazing. Starts outside the tramline, and it's well within it by the time it reaches the crease. By this time, Iftikhar has just left it alone, playing the initial line. Amazing stuff

short_text: Bumrah to Iftikhar Ahmed, no run
commentary: into the pitch again, seam-up this time, outside off. Sneaks under the bat as Iftikhar attempts to pull

short_text: Bumrah to Iftikhar Ahmed, 1 leg bye
commentary: full-toss at thigh height, angling into leg stump. Swiped down to fine leg. Oh, only thigh pad on it.

short_text: Bumrah to Imad Wasim, 1 run
commentary: looks to make room again, and slaps this length ball - which is just over the top of off - to the man at extra-cover, right on the edge of the circle. Late to take off for the single, and he ambles in as Bumrah collects the throw and back-flicks into the stumps, and he's juust in when the bails glash
pre_text: Just two off the over so far. One off the bat.

short_text: Bumrah to Iftikhar Ahmed, OUT
commentary: gone, Bumrah strikes with a full-toss, and Arshdeep takes a terrific catch despite almost running into Suryakumar Yadav! Full-toss angling into the batter, about thigh high, and he swings hard at it while cramped for room. Top-edges it high into the sky, and Arshdeep, from fine leg, and SKY, from deep square leg, converge towards the ball, and almost, almost collide. Arshdeep keeps his eyes locked on the ball and catches it nervelessly
dismissal: Iftikhar Ahmed c Arshdeep Singh b Bumrah 5 (14m 9b 0x4 0x6) SR: 55.55

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Imad Wasim, OUT
commentary: what's happened here? Arshdeep followed Imad's movement towards the leg side with a blockhole ball, and it goes through to the keeper. It's given out on field, and Imad has reviewed it. Let's figure out what happened here. Yorker slips between bat and back pad as Imad jams his bat down. Did the ball hit the inside edge? Did the bat hit the ground? Ultra Edge suggests it's inside edge, and there's daylight between the toe of the bat and the ground. Well, then, Pakistan are seven down!
pre_text: Pakistan need 18 off the last over, and Imad is on strike to Arshdeep. Left-arm over.
dismissal: Imad Wasim c †Pant b Arshdeep Singh 15 (40m 23b 1x4 0x6) SR: 65.21

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Naseem Shah, 1 run
commentary: full, slanting across, driven to the left of long-off
pre_text: Here's Naseem Shah. Shaheen, already in, is at 0 off 0 at the other end. Arshdeep stays over the wicket.

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Shaheen Shah Afridi, 1 leg bye
commentary: bit of reverse? Looked to veer in late. Yorker, hits the back leg on the full as Shaheen looks to step leg side and somehow whip it away. Rolls away into the short leg region

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Naseem Shah, FOUR
commentary: wow, Naseem Shah! Terrific shot from the No. 10! Steps across, expecting the attempted yorker at the stumps, and Arshdeep delivers what he expects. Meets it on the full, and scoops it over the keeper, and it runs away despite Siraj's chase from short fine
pre_text: 16 off 3.

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Naseem Shah, FOUR
commentary: and he slices it up in the air, and briefly it seems as though it may carry all the way... Full, slantin g away from off stump, and he slices it up and away, to the right of Kohli at deep backward point. Dives to his right, but can't stop it, but all India will worry about is that it bounced before it reached the boundary
pre_text: Two sixes needed...

short_text: Arshdeep Singh to Naseem Shah, 1 run
commentary: and he does his bit. Low full-toss on off stump, jabbed back down the ground, past the other end, and India have defended 119. What a performance, and what a match this has been
pre_text: All India need now is for Arshdeep to not bowl a wide or no-ball.
